Parent Testimonial from Worthing: May 2025
Just a little note to say how much I appreciate the time and care you have put into working with TS over the last few terms. TS really struggled with the transition to high school, which resulted in him coming to APC. The time and care you have all shown towards him...

Here at West Sussex Alternative Provision College (WSAPC) we operate in 7 separate locations, strategically sited to offer educational provision across West Sussex.
The college was formed in April 2013 and is led by me, Doug Thomas, Executive Head Teacher, Jemma Lyons, Director of Learning and Sam Channon, Chief Operations Officer. We work closely with the Governing Body, and in partnership with West Sussex schools and professional agencies. We provide appropriate primary and secondary learning provision for a range of vulnerable and challenging students.
We provide the equivalent of 292 full time places for children and young people from West Sussex who have been permanently excluded, those at risk of exclusion and those out of school for medical reasons.
All our Centres offer educational programmes for young people. Additionally, our Blended Learning Team offers educational support in a child’s home, providing personalized learning packages suitable to the circumstances and needs of the young person. Our Inclusion Team works with our colleagues in mainstream schools, to help support and develop educational strategies for children presenting with challenging behaviour and who are consequently at risk of exclusion.
At WSAPC we strive to give our pupils a fresh approach to learning in our alternative provision setting. We encourage our pupils to continue their educational progress both within the time they are with us and when they are ready to move on to other schools and establishments.
We firmly believe that education is a lifelong process and acknowledge that there may have been obstacles and past events that have blocked our pupils’ educational progress. With this in mind, we recognise that we need to address both the social and emotional needs of our pupils alongside and in conjunction with their educational needs.
We look forward at all times, confronting the obstacles to learning and then moving on and planning for a positive future.
I would like to welcome you all to our school and to say that whether you are a pupil, a parent/carer or someone who would like to visit us, you are most welcome and do hope that your experience reflects what all of us feel about working at WSAPC.

Parent Testimonial from Worthing: May 2025
TS really struggled with the transition to high school, which resulted in him coming to APC. The time and care you have all shown towards him has really made an incredible difference: He’s now confident and happy, with his anxieties about school minimised. I was originally apprehensive about TS attending APC and how it would affect him. But, I have to say, it’s been a complete surprise. He has enjoyed all his lessons and loved the physical side – especially boxing with Steve, which he will continue with once he’s left APC. He has learnt so many new skills, which he will take away and use regularly.
The support you have all shown is amazing, not just towards TS but also to me. Knowing I could call at any point and would always be met with a positive response plus having good lines of communication with you all – and not just the teaching staff. TS has built strong bonds with everyone and this has really helped him to open up.
Part of me is a little sad he’s leaving APC. You have all been really amazing, and I’m hoping all the hard work will pay off, with the rest of TS’s high school years continuing to be calm and happy.
